title: Opportunity-gated trace prefetch + weighted tail retention
creator: Ethan Walker
description:
Background: Our end-to-end tracing pipeline is a major source of CPU and allocation pressure on the inference hotpath. Prior work reduced sampling noise, but we still see disproportionate cost from preparing and serializing trace metadata for requests that do not become part of useful tail analysis. Goal: reduce hotpath tracing overhead while preserving the statistical fidelity of tail/trouble traces (p99+p999 latency/error scenarios) for debugging and RCA.

Proposal summary: Implement an "opportunity-gated trace prefetcher" that performs a low-cost heuristic probe on the hotpath to decide whether to eagerly capture extra context and/or flag a trace for heavyweight capture. The probe is intentionally cheap (few integer ops + a 64-bit bloom/LCG probe) and stores a small ephemeral token in the request context. For probes that cross an importance threshold we: 1) capture lightweight sketch metadata (constant small allocation), 2) attach an amplification weight to preserve sampling bias when reconstructing tail distributions, and 3) defer full span/body serialization to an async worker or sidecar unless the request is 100% sampled. The system uses importance-weighted resampling so the analytics backend can unbiasedly re-weight observed tails.

Design details: - Prefilter: configurable modular hook in ingress (nginx/Envoy plugin or runtime middleware). The hook computes: latency-prioritization score (route history + L7 hints), error-likelihood score (status or early signals), and a randomized gate based on a per-route maintained reservoir. - Token: a 16B token (trace-id + gate flags + weight bucket id) attached to request headers; if token is absent the hotpath avoids allocations for full span objects. - Deferred encoder: when a token indicates heavy-capture, the hotpath stores only a pointer to the minimal context and enqueues a background job for full encoding. The encoder runs outside the latency-critical goroutine so allocations/JSON encoding are amortized. - Weighting: each captured trace carries a small integer weight (1..255) that indicates how many nominal requests it represents. The analytics pipeline will use weights to compute unbiased tail percentiles. - Config knobs: per-route base-sample-rate, amplification multiplier for suspected tail signals, reservoir-size limit, soft fallback to full-sample for customer-critical routes.

Success criteria / metrics: - Hotpath allocations for trace capture reduced by >=55% on median traffic across p95 services. - Captured tail events (p99+p999) retain >=95% recall relative to baseline full-sample experiment (measured with shadowing). - End-to-end 99th percentile trace ingestion backlog increase <= 10% during rollout. - No measurable increase in user-visible tail latency beyond noise (within existing SLO error margins).

Implementation plan: 1) Prototype prefilter inside the local ingress middleware (server-side experiment) and run shadow comparison on internal staging for three weeks. 2) Implement deferred encoder backed by an async job queue with bounded concurrency (K8s job pool). 3) Add importance-weight header and analytics adapter changes to runtime metrics pipeline (requires minor changes to ingestion consumer to respect weight field). 4) Run canary on non-critical orgs with automatic rollback hooks.

Rollout plan: shadow -> 5% canary (48h) -> 25% (72h) -> 50% (one week) -> 100% (gradual). Each step gated by automatic health checks (tracing capture recall, CPU/alloc regressions, and ingestion backlog).

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: weighting mistakes could bias tail estimates. Mitigation: start with conservative amplification, run side-by-side with existing sampling for statistical validation. - Risk: background encoder backlog bursts may spike memory. Mitigation: bounded queue with drop-on-overflow and emergency fallback to minimal sketch and high weight. - Risk: additional complexity in ingestion consumers. Mitigation: keep weight field optional and backward compatible; rollout adapter in analytics first.

Artifacts & links: - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Opportunistic+Trace+Prefetcher - Prototype PR (ingress hook): https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/3145 - Deferred encoder + queue PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1287 - Analytics adapter changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/622 - Benchmark notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xOpPrefetchBench - Dashboards: Grafana dash (shadow compare): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs-shadow/trace-prefetch-shadow

2026-02-22 - Review feedback from observability eng (L. Nguyen): asked to add deterministic replay keys to aid debugs; agreed and added 8B replay nonce to token.
2026-03-01 - Benchmarks (staging): 58% reduction in hotpath allocations, CPU reduction ~22% under p95 load. Tail recall measured at 96% vs full-sample baseline (good). Detailed numbers in bench doc.
2026-03-04 - Security review: SSO and KMS not required for token; confirmed by security (A. Patel). Marked security_review_required=false.
2026-03-07 - PR 3145 opened for ingress hook. Requesting reviewers: @rachel, @mohit, @louis. Notes: added experiment flags and runtime knobs.
2026-03-09 - Integration issue discovered: analytics consumer ignores weight header on older consumer instances. Created follow-up ENG-612346 to coordinate rolling adapter changes.
